analysis.title: Four Takeaways for the Midterm Elections
key_insights: Morgan Stanley expects the midterms to yield little legislative policy variance. Executive-led policy (tariffs, trade, deregulation, immigration, export controls) stays with the White House in every outcome. The election-sensitive items are fiscal: timing of scheduled SNAP and Medicaid cuts, defense spending, and the severity of shutdown and debt-limit standoffs.

Three scenarios are framed: unified Republican control, a robust (cohesive) Democratic majority that can use must-pass bills as leverage, and a fragile Democratic majority that is divided and mostly gridlocked. Prediction market odds cited are 7% for an R House and R Senate, 61% for a D House and D Senate, and 31% for a D House and R Senate.

The midterms are not read as a 2028 signal. If Democrats outperform, the market may price a higher chance of a Democratic presidency and question the durability of deregulation and the OBBBA. Morgan Stanley calls that reaction misplaced because midterms do not typically produce outsized over- or under-performance in the following 3-6 months and the president keeps veto power for two years.

Midterm issues do not reliably carry over to presidential races. Of six midterm-to-presidential pairs since 1994, about two of the top three issues reappear, the top-ranked issue changed in five of six, and the decisive issue was visible at the prior midterm in only two of six.

Four debates are flagged for 2028 signals: social security and fiscal (Senate races in ME, MI, TX, NH), individual taxes (California one-time 5% billionaire wealth tax versus NC and OK tax-relief measures), data center restrictions, and healthcare (single payer versus public option, with El-Sayed in Michigan as the test case).

AI sentiment is assessed on two vectors. Data center opposition is a clear midterm catalyst, but mostly at the state and local level. AI safety and regulation are not driven by the election because comprehensive legislation likely needs a high-salience incident and would be bipartisan.

Data center sentiment is expected to be most constructive under a Republican sweep, broadly neutral under divided government, and least constructive under a Democratic sweep. The base case is a conditional buildout that preserves expected capex levels but only in regions contingent on community engagement or mitigation. No federal pause is expected given the national-security framing and likely presidential veto.

The binding levers on data center construction are state and local: interconnection, large-load rate design, siting, permitting and tax abatements. Governors, utility commissions and legislatures matter more than Senate races. Most candidates have converged on restrictions, with the argument now pause versus conditions, and tax breaks are the consensus target regardless of who wins.

For US equities, seasonality turns supportive from October, with scope for a near-term move lower if Democrats outperform. The type of majority matters more than which party wins. A cohesive Democratic majority can use must-pass legislation to defer OBBBA-related cuts, which helps consumer and healthcare stocks.

Rates: coupon auction sizes should rise in every outcome, so only deficits larger than investors expect should move the curve. Unified Republican control keeps a party-line reconciliation bill available (FY27 defense request, tax extension), which is the main upside risk to Treasury borrowing. Extra issuance is expected in the 2-7 year sector, cheapening the belly and flattening 5s30s.

A cohesive Democratic majority closes the reconciliation route and shifts focus to the front end, with the December funding deadline and the 2027 debt limit as leverage. A fragile majority brings the least supply pressure, lower rate volatility and potentially lower long-end yields, but also the clearest growth downside from shutdown risk.

FX: unified Republican control offers the most dollar upside via higher 2-7 year US yields and nominal growth, with short EUR/USD and short EUR/AUD performing well. A cohesive Democratic majority gives the dollar little direction, and Morgan Stanley sees value in long-dated USD optionality in CNY, CAD and MXN given tariff and sanction risk. A fragile majority is expressed through long JPY and CHF versus high beta currencies.

Economics: little difference in outlook across scenarios. A cohesive Democratic majority could add a couple of tenths to 2027 GDP and consumption if SNAP and Medicaid cuts are scaled back. A Republican win could add modestly via larger defense spending. A narrow Democratic win carries growth downside from shutdowns.

Sector heat map: Republican win favors defense, financials, nuclear and fossil energy, and data center REITs. Democratic sweep favors consumer staples, healthcare services and managed care, and renewables. Divided government is the most favorable relative outcome for data center REITs and managed care. Pharma and biotech benefit if MFN codification is less likely under either Democratic outcome.

EM sovereign credit: a Republican win is a slight positive for LatAm sovereigns close to President Trump (Argentina, Venezuela, Ecuador, El Salvador, Colombia). Other outcomes are a slight negative for those relying on unorthodox support such as the Argentina swap line and Venezuela oil deal, but practical impact is limited because executive powers are largely out of scope.

Munis are the exception to gridlock. State and local ballot measures matter for California (wealth tax and capital flight risk), Washington State (repeal of a millionaire's tax) and Florida (property tax cuts that could force local government downgrades). A cohesive Democratic majority deferring SNAP and Medicaid cuts would help state finances.

Four catalysts could mark a peak in anti-data center sentiment: incumbents winning and reverting to pro-DC positions, positive AI breakthroughs improving public perception, a Chinese capability leap shifting priorities toward geopolitics, and visible local economic benefits. Virginia's 2026 compromise and Indiana's HB 1333 are cited as templates.

If AI capex falls short, Morgan Stanley sees it weighing on growth (0.60 percentage points of 2027 GDP growth tied to AI capex), strengthening the position of hyperscalers that own compute, hurting AI adopters, and possibly easing credit spread widening because issuance would fall.

AI labor disruption is modest but increasingly visible. Unemployment in highly AI-exposed occupations is about 0.5 percentage points above the cyclical-adjusted level, up from about 0.3 points in December 2025, and the effect is clearest for workers aged 22-27. A congressional response to AI job loss is not expected over the next two years.

Exhibit 23 maps five frontier AI policy scenarios to stocks, including slower frontier model releases, higher cyber investment (CRWD, PANW, OKTA beneficiaries), US support for frontier labs, data center backlash favoring behind-the-meter power providers (BE, VST, GEV, NEE and others) and powered shell providers (CIFR, WULF, HUT, RIOT, GLXY), and restrictive legislation after the elections.

Model and tech restrictions are expected to stay executive-led (OFAC, Entity List, IEEPA), with Congress able to make them durable through the NDAA, potentially via the AI OVERWATCH Act and the MATCH Act. A middle path is expected: open-weight models permitted below the frontier, with controls at the frontier.

Policy proposals tracked under a Democratic sweep include the Klobuchar-Cruz-Thune frontier AI safety draft, four House bills in the National Data Center Plan, the AI Kill Switch Act (introduced July 2026) and the AI LEAD Act (proposed September 2026). A tax on compute is viewed as a 2028-29 priority. Nationwide data center moratoriums are considered unlikely.

Kalshi prediction markets are described as a useful addition to the macro toolkit. Their fed funds and CPI forecast accuracy outperforms common indicators, and GDP, NFP and unemployment accuracy is in line with traditional indicators. Morgan Stanley has not yet extended the analysis to election markets.

Morgan Stanley's equity strategists note historical post-midterm returns of roughly +22% over 12 months and say slowing earnings growth suggests more modest gains than recent years. Defensives have typically outperformed ahead of midterms, followed by growth, cyclical and small-cap outperformance after the election.

sector_views.rationale: Positive in a Republican win on fossil and nuclear expansion and a deregulation bias. A cohesive Democratic sweep is more supportive for renewables. Status quo under divided government.
Defense spending growth is most likely under unified Republican control. In either Democratic scenario spending growth continues but is more negotiated.
Continued deregulation under a Republican win supports growth, capital deployment and capital markets activity. Oversight under divided government may slow but not derail regulatory easing.

sector_views.sector: Consumer Staples / Hardlines / Broadlines / Food Retail
sector_views.rationale: SNAP cuts weigh on low-income demand if implemented as legislated. Delay of cuts under Democratic outcomes limits downside.

Divided government reduces the prospect of major policy changes in Medicare Advantage, Medicaid and ACA, giving stability and earnings visibility for managed care. A Democratic sweep could roll back potential Medicaid changes.
MFN codification is possible under a Republican win and unlikely under either Democratic outcome. Potential 340B and PBM reform has bipartisan support and is the main investor focus.
Republican win carries higher risk of expiration of refundable tax credits that weigh on lower-income demand. Democratic sweep improves low-end demand resilience, benefiting QSR.

Republican win brings easier permitting and energy access. Divided government is the most favorable relative outcome for pricing power. A Democratic sweep raises costs, which favors scaled incumbents.

macro_indicators.indicator: US federal deficit as share of GDP
macro_indicators.reading: around 6% over the next two years
macro_indicators.interpretation: Morgan Stanley's baseline. A Republican win adds about 0.2pp of upside risk in 2027 via defense spending, and a unified Democratic sweep could add about 0.2pp through delayed SNAP and Medicaid cuts. Deficit contraction is unlikely in any scenario.

macro_indicators.reading: 2.3% in 2027, with 0.60 percentage points tied to AI-related capex net of imports
macro_indicators.interpretation: A politically constrained AI buildout would weigh on growth and could dampen sentiment and consumption through lower asset prices.
Delaying SNAP and Medicaid cuts adds roughly $130 billion if both slip a year, which is small against this deficit.

macro_indicators.reading: near $1.3 trillion across fiscal 2027 and 2028 at current auction sizes
macro_indicators.interpretation: Larger coupon auctions are expected in every outcome. Bill share of marketable debt sits near 22% versus 14% before the pandemic.

macro_indicators.indicator: Contribution of AI disruption to aggregate unemployment rate
macro_indicators.interpretation: A noticeable but modest effect. Highly exposed occupations account for about 30% of employment.

crypto_views: Powered shell providers with crypto mining roots (CIFR, WULF, HUT, RIOT, GLXY, MARA, APLD) are tied to data center buildout policy. Morgan Stanley rates MARA Underweight and CIFR, HUT, RIOT, WULF Overweight in its coverage tables.
Crypto regulation is listed among policy areas with potential for compromise, but the report gives no crypto market view.

trade_ideas.description: Own long-dated USD optionality in CNY, CAD and MXN
trade_ideas.rationale: A White House blocked in Congress may lean harder on tariffs and sanctions, which may be selectively USD supportive when narrowly targeted.

trade_ideas.description: Long JPY and CHF versus high beta currencies (AUD, NOK, GBP) in a fragile Democratic majority outcome
trade_ideas.rationale: Yields offer the least dollar support but growth risk points the other way, so Morgan Stanley would express this through long JPY and CHF versus high beta rather than a dollar view.

trade_ideas.description: Short EUR/USD and short EUR/AUD in a unified Republican control outcome
trade_ideas.rationale: Unified control offers the most upside to 2-7 year US yields and a stronger nominal US growth impulse, which boosts the USD, commodity prices and risk demand.
trade_ideas.risk: Treasury and the Ministry of Finance intervention may limit USD/JPY gains.

trade_ideas.description: Belly of the Treasury curve cheapens and 5s30s flattens in a unified Republican control outcome
trade_ideas.rationale: Additional issuance from wider deficits lands in the 2-7 year sector, while AI-related corporate supply sets the marginal price of duration at the long end.
trade_ideas.risk: Only deficits larger than investors currently expect should move the curve.

risk_factors: A Democratic outperformance surprise could trigger a near-term equity selloff and higher perceived odds of a Democratic presidency in 2028
Shutdowns and debt-limit standoffs, with the December funding deadline and 2027 debt limit as pressure points
Treasury supply upside from a Republican-led reconciliation bill carrying the FY27 defense request and tax extensions
Anti-data center challengers winning state and local races, slowing permitting and construction
Shift in public opposition toward AI safety concerns, which could remove the need for a high-salience incident before legislation
A major AI risk event that pauses AI adoption
A White House leaning harder on tariffs and sanctions
Capital flight and tax-base effects from state ballot measures in California, Washington and Florida
Medicare for All reviving as a credible 2028 theme if single-payer candidates win large margins
vol_and_positioning: Narrower legislative variance under a fragile Democratic majority argues for lower rate volatility.
Equity market reaction to executive headlines shows diminishing sensitivity over time. Treasuries saw more selloff days after posts with clear macro read-across.

A Democratic outperformance surprise could cause a near-term equity move lower that Morgan Stanley thinks is unlikely to be sustained. Uncertainty from a change in control is compared to 2022 midterm volatility.
For the 2027 debt limit, bills maturing around the x-date have cheapened most consistently across a decade of episodes.
geopolitical: US-China tech divergence and sovereign AI, with the executive branch expected to lead on restricting Chinese access to advanced AI capabilities and chips
Argentina swap line via the Treasury Exchange Stabilization Fund and the Venezuela oil deal via OFAC licensing, both outside the appropriations process
US-Iran conflict and Truth Social tariff posts cited as sources of headline risk, with diminishing equity market sensitivity
Japan's Treasury and Ministry of Finance said they will not hesitate to intervene again after the July 31 operation, which may limit USD/JPY gains
Possible White House reliance on tariffs and sanctions if blocked in Congress

tension_points.bull_case: Morgan Stanley argues any selloff on Democratic outperformance is misplaced and unlikely to be sustained because midterms do not typically drive outsized market performance in the following 3-6 months and the president keeps veto power for two years.
tension_points.bear_case: Markets may price a higher chance of a Democratic presidency in 2028 and question the durability of deregulation and the OBBBA, creating regime uncertainty that weighs on index-level prices, similar to 2022 midterm volatility.

tension_points.theme: Data center buildout under midterm outcomes
tension_points.bull_case: Incumbents win against anti-data center challengers and a Republican sweep raises odds of federal support through permitting reform, generation additions and siting on federal land, so pro-DC incumbents revert and moratoriums lift.
tension_points.bear_case: Anti-data center challengers win state and local seats and Democrats sweep, so moratoriums take longer to reverse and federal restrictions in 2029 become a rising tail risk.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A sea change of anti-data center lawmakers winning at the state and local level in key races such as Texas and Pennsylvania would break the constructive base case.

tension_points.bull_case: Comprehensive AI regulation is unlikely near term, action stays voluntary and executive-led, and the midterms are not a driver of a government response.
tension_points.bear_case: A high-salience AI incident or a shift in public opposition toward safety could allow bipartisan legislation attached to a must-pass vehicle such as appropriations or the NDAA.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Voters prioritizing safety concerns over utility bills, water and NIMBYism, or a major AI risk event that pauses adoption.

theme_stances.key_argument: Data center sentiment is most constructive under a Republican sweep, neutral under divided government and weakest under a Democratic sweep.
theme_stances.evidence: data center sentiment most likely positive in a Republican sweep

theme_stances.key_argument: Tariffs, trade, deregulation, immigration and export controls sit with the White House and continue regardless of the midterm outcome.
theme_stances.evidence: What the midterms won't change: the executive-led agenda.

theme_stances.key_argument: Comprehensive AI regulation needs a high-salience incident and the midterms are not the driver.
theme_stances.evidence: comprehensive AI regulation is unlikely in the near term absent a high salience incident
